front_blocks.md: Define oxidation in terms of oxygen.

back_blocks.md: Oxidation is the **gain** of oxygen by an element or compound during a chemical reaction.

cards.front_md: Define oxidation in terms of oxygen.
cards.back_md: Oxidation is the **gain** of oxygen by an element or compound during a chemical reaction.

front_blocks.md: Define reduction in terms of oxygen.

back_blocks.md: Reduction is the **loss** of oxygen from an element or compound during a chemical reaction.

cards.front_md: Define reduction in terms of oxygen.
cards.back_md: Reduction is the **loss** of oxygen from an element or compound during a chemical reaction.

front_blocks.md: In the reaction between zinc oxide and carbon, zinc oxide is **..........** because it loses oxygen, while carbon is **..........** because it gains oxygen.

back_blocks.md: In the reaction between zinc oxide and carbon, zinc oxide is **reduced** because it loses oxygen, while carbon is **oxidised** because it gains oxygen.

cards.front_md: In the reaction between zinc oxide and carbon, zinc oxide is **..........** because it loses oxygen, while carbon is **..........** because it gains oxygen.
cards.back_md: In the reaction between zinc oxide and carbon, zinc oxide is **reduced** because it loses oxygen, while carbon is **oxidised** because it gains oxygen.

front_blocks.md: In a redox reaction, oxidation and reduction occur in separate reactions at different times.

back_blocks.md: In a redox reaction, oxidation and reduction occur **simultaneously** in the same reaction. One species gains oxygen while another loses oxygen at the same time.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

In a redox reaction, oxidation and reduction occur in separate reactions at different times.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

In a redox reaction, oxidation and reduction occur **simultaneously** in the same reaction. One species gains oxygen while another loses oxygen at the same time.

front_blocks.md: What information does the Roman numeral in the name of a transition metal compound provide?

back_blocks.md: The Roman numeral gives the **oxidation number** (charge) of the transition metal ion in that compound. For example, iron(III) indicates that the iron ion has a **3+ charge**, Fe<sup>3+</sup>.

cards.front_md: What information does the Roman numeral in the name of a transition metal compound provide?
cards.back_md: The Roman numeral gives the **oxidation number** (charge) of the transition metal ion in that compound. For example, iron(III) indicates that the iron ion has a **3+ charge**, Fe<sup>3+</sup>.

front_blocks.md: Iron(II) oxide has the formula **..........** and contains Fe<sup>2+</sup> ions, while iron(III) oxide has the formula **..........** and contains Fe<sup>3+</sup> ions.

back_blocks.md: Iron(II) oxide has the formula **FeO** and contains Fe<sup>2+</sup> ions, while iron(III) oxide has the formula **Fe**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**<sub>**3**</sub> and contains Fe<sup>3+</sup> ions.

cards.front_md: Iron(II) oxide has the formula **..........** and contains Fe<sup>2+</sup> ions, while iron(III) oxide has the formula **..........** and contains Fe<sup>3+</sup> ions.
cards.back_md: Iron(II) oxide has the formula **FeO** and contains Fe<sup>2+</sup> ions, while iron(III) oxide has the formula **Fe**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**<sub>**3**</sub> and contains Fe<sup>3+</sup> ions.

back_blocks.md: **Fe**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**<sub>**3**</sub> is reduced because it loses oxygen to form iron, **Fe**.

cards.back_md: **Fe**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**<sub>**3**</sub> is reduced because it loses oxygen to form iron, **Fe**.

back_blocks.md: **CO** is oxidised because it gains oxygen to form **CO**<sub>**2**</sub>.

cards.back_md: **CO** is oxidised because it gains oxygen to form **CO**<sub>**2**</sub>.

front_blocks.md: State what OIL RIG stands for in the context of redox reactions.

back_blocks.md: OIL RIG is a mnemonic: **Oxidation Is Loss** (of electrons) and **Reduction Is Gain** (of electrons). It summarises the electron transfer definitions of oxidation and reduction.

cards.front_md: State what OIL RIG stands for in the context of redox reactions.
cards.back_md: OIL RIG is a mnemonic: **Oxidation Is Loss** (of electrons) and **Reduction Is Gain** (of electrons). It summarises the electron transfer definitions of oxidation and reduction.

front_blocks.md: In a redox reaction, the species that is oxidised loses electrons and its oxidation number increases.

back_blocks.md: When a species is oxidised it loses electrons, which causes its oxidation number to increase. For example, Fe loses electrons to become Fe<sup>2+</sup>, so its oxidation number increases from 0 to +2.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

In a redox reaction, the species that is oxidised loses electrons and its oxidation number increases.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

When a species is oxidised it loses electrons, which causes its oxidation number to increase. For example, Fe loses electrons to become Fe<sup>2+</sup>, so its oxidation number increases from 0 to +2.

front_blocks.md: In the reaction Fe + Cu<sup>2+</sup> → Fe<sup>2+</sup> + Cu, iron is **..........** because it **..........** electrons, and Cu<sup>2+</sup> is **..........** because it **..........** electrons.

back_blocks.md: In the reaction Fe + Cu<sup>2+</sup> → Fe<sup>2+</sup> + Cu, iron is **oxidised** because it **loses** electrons, and Cu<sup>2+</sup> is **reduced** because it **gains** electrons.

cards.front_md: In the reaction Fe + Cu<sup>2+</sup> → Fe<sup>2+</sup> + Cu, iron is **..........** because it **..........** electrons, and Cu<sup>2+</sup> is **..........** because it **..........** electrons.
cards.back_md: In the reaction Fe + Cu<sup>2+</sup> → Fe<sup>2+</sup> + Cu, iron is **oxidised** because it **loses** electrons, and Cu<sup>2+</sup> is **reduced** because it **gains** electrons.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of the oxidising agent in a redox reaction?

back_blocks.md: The oxidising agent **accepts electrons** from another species. In doing so, it is itself **reduced** (its oxidation number decreases).

cards.front_md: What is the role of the oxidising agent in a redox reaction?
cards.back_md: The oxidising agent **accepts electrons** from another species. In doing so, it is itself **reduced** (its oxidation number decreases).

front_blocks.md: What is the role of the reducing agent in a redox reaction?

back_blocks.md: The reducing agent **donates electrons** to another species. In doing so, it is itself **oxidised** (its oxidation number increases).

cards.front_md: What is the role of the reducing agent in a redox reaction?
cards.back_md: The reducing agent **donates electrons** to another species. In doing so, it is itself **oxidised** (its oxidation number increases).

front_blocks.md: In the half-equation Ag → Ag<sup>+</sup> + e<sup>-</sup>, silver is **..........** because it **..........** an electron.

back_blocks.md: In the half-equation Ag → Ag<sup>+</sup> + e<sup>-</sup>, silver is **oxidised** because it **loses** an electron.

cards.front_md: In the half-equation Ag → Ag<sup>+</sup> + e<sup>-</sup>, silver is **..........** because it **..........** an electron.
cards.back_md: In the half-equation Ag → Ag<sup>+</sup> + e<sup>-</sup>, silver is **oxidised** because it **loses** an electron.

front_blocks.md: In the half-equation O<sub>2</sub> + 4e<sup>-</sup> → 2O<sup>2-</sup>, oxygen is **..........** because it **..........** electrons.

back_blocks.md: In the half-equation O<sub>2</sub> + 4e<sup>-</sup> → 2O<sup>2-</sup>, oxygen is **reduced** because it **gains** electrons.

cards.front_md: In the half-equation O<sub>2</sub> + 4e<sup>-</sup> → 2O<sup>2-</sup>, oxygen is **..........** because it **..........** electrons.
cards.back_md: In the half-equation O<sub>2</sub> + 4e<sup>-</sup> → 2O<sup>2-</sup>, oxygen is **reduced** because it **gains** electrons.

front_blocks.md: How do you identify which species has been oxidised in the ionic equation V<sup>3+</sup> + Fe<sup>3+</sup> → V<sup>4+</sup> + Fe<sup>2+</sup>?

back_blocks.md: V<sup>3+</sup> is **oxidised** because it **loses one electron** to become V<sup>4+</sup>, increasing its oxidation number from +3 to +4. Fe<sup>3+</sup> is reduced because it gains one electron to become Fe<sup>2+</sup>.
